Posterior class probabilities and class membership

classify.Rd

classify() returns one row per input row, aligned with the data the model was fitted to: posterior probabilities p1, ..., pK and the most likely class, ready to cbind() to the data. posterior() returns the posterior probabilities of the analysed rows only.

Usage

classify(object, level = c("within", "between"))

posterior(object, wave = 1, level = c("within", "between"))

Arguments

object

A fitted latentmix model.

level

Two-level models only: "within" (individuals, default) or "between" (clusters).

wave

For an LTA, the wave (1 = first).

Value

classify(): a data frame with columns row (row number in the input data), p1, ..., pK and class (integer); for level = "between", cluster instead of row. posterior(): a numeric matrix with columns p1, ..., pK and one row per analysed row (per cluster for level = "between").

Details

Rows with every indicator missing were not analysed: in classify() their probabilities and class are NA. For an LTA, classify() refers to the first wave; use posterior(m, wave = t) for wave t. The matrices are transferred from Julia through a temporary binary file, which is fast for large samples.

For a two-level model (lca() / lpa() with level2), level = "within" (default) gives the within-class posterior of every row given all data of its cluster, and level = "between" one row per cluster (column cluster, the cluster label) with the between-class posterior and modal between class.

See also

predict(), classification_table()

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# add posterior class probabilities and the modal ACE class to the data
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)     # 4 ACE classes, as generated
#> Starting Julia ...
cl <- classify(m)
aces2 <- cbind(aces, cl[-1])
table(aces2$class)   # modal class sizes
#> 
#>   1   2   3   4 
#> 876 262 212 150 
# mean depressive symptoms by modal class (naive; bch() corrects for misclassification)
tapply(aces2$depress, aces2$class, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
#>         1         2         3         4 
#>  5.039007  9.941176  7.449275 12.882759 
# }
